subject: Error in vecseq - unless applying unique()

messages.author: f1fed04b6e17838b
messages.subject: Error in vecseq - unless applying unique()
parts:
Hi Altuna,
I'm using your package for RRBSeq analysis and in the near future will move to WGBSSeq.
Trying to run your pieces of code I also faced the above error. 
The RefSeq BED file has been downloaded from UCSC website (see below)

At the very first time, attempting to run unite() over promoters' Granges I got the error and then successfully fixed by installing development version (0.9.4 ; with data.table 1.9.4).

Happy with that I moved to the same enrichment analysis over exons and introns. Again the vecseq error.
Looked to BS ratio files, but, as expected no duplicated coordinates (since it worked fine before)
Looking  over the bed file I saw many exons/introns should count more than once for the same coordinates given the presence of splicing variants (but I would assume for promoters too, though).
Looking over the web I found that one can remove duplicate by applying the unique() function over the Granges object. After that unite() seems to work.

So the question: I'm using a regular USCS bed file with RefSeq info and its intrinsic redundancy, but the software does not work unless tweaking around the Granges objects.

Is this what you really wanted to be?. Is your code expected to handle duplicated exons/introns/promoters given by alternative spliced genes? Am I doing something wrong. Using a wrong BED file?

BED file has been downloaded from UCSC as follow

  • http://genome.ucsc.edu/cgi-bin/hgTables?command=start
  • selected hg19
  • Genes and gene predictions -> RefSeq genes
  • table: RefGene
  • format: BED - browser extensible format

Hope you can find time to answer. Nice work with this tool!

Best Regards

Davide

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Error in vecseq - unless applying unique()
parts:
Hi Davide,
it should be able to deal with refseq annotations that have the same id but mapping the different chr_start_end coordinates. It won't be able to deal with other issues where refseq ids are the same, chr, start,end coordinates are the same but there is internal alternative splicing. If you send me the exact file you used and the commands, I will see if it is a bug or something expected by design. it would be good to share the sessionInfo() as well.

Best
Altuna
